content.title: About
content.content: Ranch dip is a creamy sauce made from yogurt and seasoned with classic Ranch spices: garlic, onion, dill, parsley and dried milk powders. It has a mild, slightly tangy flavor with herbal notes and works well as a dip for vegetables, chips and crackers.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ranch is one of the most popular sauces in the US, with consumption exceeding 1.5 billion servings per year.
The original Ranch dressing was created in the 1950s in Alabama as a salad topping.
A yogurt‑based version appeared in the 2000s to offer a lighter alternative to the traditional mayo‑based Ranch.
The blend of herbs and garlic makes the sauce versatile for many cuisines—from American to Mexican.
In Russia, Ranch dip is often sold in ready‑to‑eat plastic containers.

items.title: Rich in probiotics
items.content: The yogurt base provides live cultures that support gut microbiota.

items.title: Lower fat content
items.content: Compared with classic mayo‑based Ranch, the yogurt version contains less saturated fat.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Yogurt is a good source of calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yogurt supplies vitamin B12 and riboflavin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Herbal antioxidants
items.content: Dill and parsley are rich in vitamin C and flavonoids with antioxidant properties.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Contains yogurt, so it may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions can be salty; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: A small amount of sugar is sometimes added for flavor balance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Ranch dip with vegetable sticks, potato wedges, crackers, chicken nuggets, or use it as a dressing for salads and burgers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 2‑4 °C in a sealed container. Once opened, it is usually good for 5‑7 days. Do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
